title: Docker Networking Overview & Drivers 🌐
description: Understand why containers need networks and meet the built‑in network drivers.

slides.title: Why Containers Need Networking 🤝
slides.content:
# The Network Is the Backbone

A container running in isolation is like a computer without a network cable. To be useful, containers need to:

- **Talk to each other** (microservices).
- **Expose services to the outside world** (web servers, APIs).
- **Reach the internet** (download packages, call external APIs).

Docker provides a full networking stack that works out‑of‑the‑box, but you can heavily customise it.

slides.title: Network Drivers – The Plumbing 🔧
slides.content:
# Docker’s Built‑In Drivers

When you install Docker, you get several network drivers:

- **bridge** – the default private virtual network for containers on a single host.
- **host** – the container shares the host’s network stack (no isolation).
- **none** – completely disables networking.
- **overlay** – connects containers across multiple Docker daemons (Swarm).
- **macvlan** – assigns a MAC address to each container, making it appear as a physical device on the network.

We’ll focus on **bridge** (both default and custom) and briefly touch the others.

quizData.question: Which network driver is the default for Docker containers?
quizData.explanation: Unless you specify otherwise, containers run on the default bridge network.

slides.title: How Docker Networking Works 🧬
slides.content:
# Virtual Switches & IP Assignment

Docker creates a virtual switch (a bridge) on the host. Each container gets a virtual Ethernet interface attached to that bridge.

- Docker’s embedded DNS server provides name resolution.
- IP addresses are assigned from a private subnet (e.g., `172.17.0.0/16` for the default bridge).
- Containers on the same bridge can communicate directly via IP.

> Think of the bridge as a virtual network switch that Docker manages for you.

slides.title: See Your Networks 📋
slides.content: List all networks on your system:
slides.codeSnippet:
docker network ls

# Output:
# NETWORK ID     NAME      DRIVER    SCOPE
# abc123def456   bridge    bridge    local
# def456abc789   host      host      local
# 789abcdef012   none      null      local

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Always Use Custom Networks

Default bridge is fine for quick tests, but custom bridge networks enable automatic DNS resolution and network isolation. We’ll create one soon!
